newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weaker on arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weaker on arbitrage play.

text.p: * Four-day swap points prompts dollar buying
The Philippine peso closed weaker at 26.312 to the dollar from Thursday's 26.299 due to arbitrage play and short-covering, traders said.
"It's a U.S. holiday on Monday, so banks get to keep their pesos for four days," one trader said. The U.S. market will be closed on Monday for Martin Luther King Day.
Deals done in the pose-dollar market are settled the next working day.
Therefore, banks which buy dollars on Friday get to keep their pesos over the weekend and earn higher interest rates.

Another trader said some foreign banks were covering their short dollar positions after they oversold their dollar holdings in the past few days. The peso opened at 26.296 and slowly crept down to 26.312 throughout the session.
Turnover was moderate at $170.10 million from Thursday's $152.80 million.
The Central Bank did not intervene in the market, pushing its offer rate higher to 26.32 from 26.30 and bid rate at 26.27.
